limitations: session_minutes@1 is not used: its minutes count KuaiRand pool videos only (median 0.06-0.2 min per session) and its contract declares no scale factor; session length stays the individual's plausible log-normal (pop.decision.session_length).

daily_return@1 has no content, notification or satisfaction inputs: whether an individual browses on a day does not respond to what platforms show (satisfaction acts through activity choice, abandonment and returns to resources); class 2 does not learn its daily engagement either (the day review steps its memory, the fitted model decides activity).
extra_sessions@1 is served as the E3 review's constant C2 rate (no individual heterogeneity in sessions per active day).

article_open_semantic@1 is a news-article model (MIND) extrapolated to the population's web page slates; its text affinity is the cosine of the individual's interests (which drift towards consumed items) with the headline, not the mean embedding of its consumed items; own topic views are tracked for the four most read topics.
customer_return@1 gives P(another order within 90 days); the day of that order is drawn from the customer's own mean gap (30 days after a first order).
Spam sites are keyword lists; rich, thin and off-topic generated sites retell the real corpus.
Class 3 roles are entrepreneurs/publishers, competitors and collaborators; researchers, engineers, employees, organisations and investors are not class-3 roles here.

Personal memory benefit in the integrated worlds is measured (SP-3.4) but not significant: most of what predicts an individual's utility is in its observation; the BPTT unit test shows the memory can carry hidden traits.

G.1 counts members whose policy stepped their memory on one day (day review or session); members that took sessions on one day are fewer (fitted daily return, about 40-60% of class-2 members per day in the small worlds).

Population-world throughput (population-only development world, CPU, warm cache): 377 simulated days per CPU-hour on this branch vs 664 at 55433e7 - the population browses ~4.7x more per day; CPU per web visit fell from 4.01 to 1.50 ms. The R6/R7 batch/event reductions did not measurably reduce CPU per visit. The D-27 targets bind the civilisation world, where the shared space's encoders, the social consumption engine and shopping searches dominate (OPTIMISATION_REQUESTS.md on c5c/w3b-perf).

Two forks of one snapshot can bill sandboxed site compute differently under heavy machine load (a fresh measurement beyond the D-20 metering tolerance is billed instead of the anchor); G.6's frozen-at-switch fork therefore shares random streams and population decisions with the main world until the first post-switch update, but not necessarily every operator's billed compute.
